text: You already know how to provision a Storage Account, a Fabric Capacity, an Event Hub — by hand, in the Azure Portal. This course teaches describing that same resource in a text file, checked into Git, applied the same way every time.
Manual provisioning works exactly once, remembered only by whoever clicked. Infrastructure as code is a text file — reviewed the same way as application code, and rebuildable from that file alone.

An Azure CLI script is imperative — a list of steps run in order, once. Terraform and Bicep are declarative — you describe the end state, and the tool figures out what needs to change. Run it again with no changes, and nothing happens.
This track's own capstone projects needed real Azure resources provisioned before a pipeline could run. IaC makes that step reviewable, repeatable, and recoverable.
Declarative, reviewable, rebuildable. Next up: choosing between Terraform and Bicep.
